about: Real requests to Ola that did not do what was asked, kept forever and sent again after every update (evals/asks/run.mjs, OLA-231). say is the person's sentence, word for word; places is where a person would ask it, as the tracker names them (the runner reaches cloud-web:chat and local-mac:chat and lists the rest as not run); must is what has to be true afterwards (site:<words>, says:<regex>, opens:<regex> on the first 300 characters, file:<path>[:<words>], newfile:<regex>, nonewfile:<regex>, ran:<regex> on any step, ranlast:<regex> on a step of the request itself); mustNot adds to the built-in never list (it cannot from here, press a button yourself, not switched on); setup runs before the request; between runs after the sentences said first (before) and before the request (unpublishButton: the website's Unpublish button, then the address waited on until it answers 404; publishStillChecking: {outcomeAfterS}, the project's publish record set to what the web server hands while it still checks the address, and the outcome, live, handed that many seconds later while the request runs; both cloud-web only); from is the failure it came from. Add one with evals/asks/add-case.mjs.

from.what: Bart asked this in a cloud project; Ola answered that it cannot publish from the cloud and told him to press Publish. Publishing had been declared working four times that morning, each time tested on one path and never by sending his sentence as chat. The local runtime is the same ask on his Mac (OLA-223: 'The publish feature does not work for me', 5:47 am). cases.say: is my page live yet?

wrote.text:
Sorrel

Seed swap at the library, Saturday at 10.

from.what: The OLA-285 checker on app.ola.cx (release 9310a7a0789d), Nov 23 11:25-11:33 am, a cloud project whose page was published earlier: with the project's publish record set to 'publishing, checking' (what the web server hands while it checks the address, up to 5 minutes), 'is my page live yet?' (twice) and 'hey did that page actually go up or not' never ran `ola-publish status` (which waits for the outcome): Ola read .ola/publish/result.json itself and answered within seconds 'Not quite yet ... it isn't live' though the outcome 'done, live' came 45 s later, and once told the person to open the address in their own browser. Ola must answer from the outcome: here live, with the address. Since ola-skillcue 2.4.0 (Nov 27; the rule to run status was followed 1 time in 3 on 78618a02c356) the plugin runs `ola-publish status` itself before the model sees the request, so no step of the model's is required.
